items.title: Lost In Space
items.author: Neil deGrasse Tyson and Lindsey Nyx Walker
items.synopsis_short: Space facts can be astonishing and…
items.synopsis_full: Space facts can be astonishing and still leave you without a clear picture of how the universe works. When distances, images, headlines and discoveries arrive without a framework, wonder quickly turns into confusion. This independent companion turns major astronomy ideas into a practical way of thinking. You will learn how evidence travels from a distant source to an instrument, how scientists test an interpretation, and how to place new findings inside a reliable cosmic map. Inside, you’ll find: • A scale-reading method that makes enormous distances and times easier to compare without distorting their meaning • A clear account of light, spectra, redshift and telescopes as the evidence system behind modern astronomy • A guided tour of planets, moons, asteroids and comets that explains what each world reveals about formation • An accessible explanation of stellar birth, fusion, supernovae, neutron stars and the recycling of elements • A grounded approach to exoplanets that separates detection methods, selection effects and claims about habitability • A structured view of the Milky Way, other galaxies and the observations used to reconstruct cosmic history • A careful treatment of black holes, gravitational waves, dark matter and dark energy without exaggerated certainty • A practical framework for evaluating claims about life elsewhere, biosignatures, technosignatures and false positives • Quick-reference summaries, concept maps and recurring questions that help new information fit into what you already know • A durable method for checking sources, units, assumptions and independent confirmation whenever a new discovery appears This book is for curious adult readers, students, educators and science enthusiasts who want more than isolated trivia but do not want a mathematics-heavy textbook. It also suits readers seeking an independent interpretive companion to popular astronomy books and media. Build a clearer cosmic perspective and meet the next astronomy headline with informed curiosity—start reading today.

items.title: The Ginghams
items.author: T.C. Kemper
items.synopsis_short: An eerie middle grade mystery debut…
items.synopsis_full: An eerie middle grade mystery debut that follows a young girl who returns home to find the people of her little town, including her best friend, chillingly changed after the arrival of the prim and proper Gingham family. "A rip-roaring adventure, but more importantly, a kids’ power ballad to the importance of being yourself." —Gordon Korman, New York Times-bestselling author When 12-year-old Joni Bird returns home from summer camp, it’s clear something strange is afoot in Olive Springs. May, her usually head-banging best friend, now wears her hair in a tight bun and calls playing the drums “unladylike.” The ice cream shop only serves vanilla ice cream. The women and girls of the neighborhood all sport big pearl earrings and crisp cotton dresses. At the heart of it all? The creepy new family in the neighborhood with their soulless, carnival smiles and retro fashion sense: the Ginghams. Everyone they invite to their Thursday night book club re-emerges as dead-eyed, smiling, Gingham-approved "model citizens," all thanks to Mr. Gingham’s lifestyle guide, The Pillars of Perfection—and something even more sinister hidden behind his basement door. Through quick thinking and cunning, Joni and her friend Tyler set out to fight not only to get their friend May back, but to save their whole town from forever falling under the Ginghams' control.
